meta.phase-name: Escape The Dungeon Asset Authoring Alignment

phase-plan.purpose: Turn docs-site into the real DungeonBreak web product: public-facing marketing for the game plus an internal customer/admin portal for content authoring, asset inspection, publishing, and test/game review. Keep the product Escape the Dungeon-first, preserve the hosted assistant workflow inside the UI, and remove leftover RepoPlanner/planning cockpit ownership from the host app so the main site can focus on game/player/admin surfaces instead of mixed tooling responsibilities.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: direct export/publish workflow, better form/asset management for current game schemas, game-specific widget/binding improvements for awkward authored fields, a hosted assistant chat bubble built with Assistant UI plus MCP/browser-assistant-friendly contracts, and a testing stack that covers unit, browser UI, deterministic E2E, and reviewable report surfaces. Asset Explorer should also own the first schema-driven media authoring loop: form fields can declare media slots, open a hosted media widget, queue ElevenLabs/OpenAI-backed generation where the backend exists, preserve video slots even before the hosted video path is wired, and round-trip generation metadata back into canonical asset JSON. Also in scope: recasting docs-site as the DungeonBreak marketing + internal portal, restricting logins to an explicit allowlist for now, and removing or relocating embedded RepoPlanner/planning pages, routes, navigation, legacy docs, old report surfaces, and legacy Payload admin/env sync utilities out of the host app so they stop taxing the main build graph. The test/game review surface should publish the latest build artifacts and summaries to GitHub Pages on every main-branch commit so the repo always has a current public review page, but that review host is separate from the real site. Prefer existing user subscriptions where possible; if that is not practical, support OpenRouter-backed models as the default hosted fallback. Out of scope: broad public multi-tenant auth, generalized multi-project productization, and diff/review governance.

file.description: Main game-facing asset authoring surface; finish export/publish workflow, keep supported Escape the Dungeon packs/forms as the default interaction model, and leave generic/manual schema creation as an advanced escape hatch instead of the primary flow.
Schema-driven media widget for Asset Explorer fields. This is the authoring-side bridge between RJSF forms and hosted image/audio/video slot management.
Generic Asset Explorer media-generation endpoint that queues hosted generation jobs and normalizes their status back into form-friendly field values.
Root marketing/portal landing page for the slimmed-down docs-site product.
Internal onboarding/login page for the allowlisted authoring portal.
Temporary internal login handoff: allowlisted email plus shared onboarding password becomes a Payload session and portal-access cookie.
Proxy gate for the internal portal and portal-bound API surfaces. This is the runtime entry point that keeps unauthenticated users out of Asset Explorer and admin.
Keep project detail and export/publish helpers aligned with Escape the Dungeon canonical forms, assets, and contract-shaped output.
Likely integration point for MCP/browser-assistant interoperability once the editor exposes toolable operations to the hosted assistant shell.
Unit and browser-oriented Vitest reporting/coverage baseline for reviewable docs-site test output.
Deterministic end-to-end and visual baseline harness for docs-site and game/content editor flows.
Current CI source of truth for docs-site/game checks and build artifacts; it should become the producer for publishable latest test/game review data.
Static review-site generator that turns the latest game/test artifacts into a GitHub Pages-friendly site bundle with links into the standalone game and HTML reports.
Project export endpoint that should be directly reachable from the new Asset Explorer workflow.
Project publish endpoint for pushing canonical pack edits back into engine/game artifacts.
Top-level route for the Escape the Dungeon-first content authoring loop.
Main app shell/navigation. This is where the host should stop advertising planning surfaces and lean into game, editor, portal, and marketing navigation.
Production-build topology and bundler settings for the slimmed-down portal. This is where the Turbopack/workspace-root/Payload externalization fix lives.
Payload config for the narrowed portal. Legacy docs/env collections and plugin surfaces should stay out of this config unless they clearly serve Asset Explorer or media generation.

task.description: Finish the direct export/publish workflow and tighten the forms/assets management flow so canonical asset editing stays tied to the playable game loop instead of a separate content page. Keep the supported Escape the Dungeon forms as the default path, and make the next action obvious: seed the form, import the canonical pack data, author assets, publish, then jump back into the latest game build.

Add the first Escape the Dungeon-specific schema/form improvements for awkward authored fields and bindings instead of growing generic schema tooling. This now explicitly includes schema-annotated media slots plus the hosted media widget/modal for image, ElevenLabs audio, and future video-backed asset fields, and it should keep supported game forms/packs visibly ahead of ad hoc manual forms in the UI.

Add a hosted assistant chat shell for Asset Explorer/content authoring using Assistant UI as an expandable bubble, with tool contracts designed for MCP/browser assistants and a model-routing strategy that prefers existing user subscriptions when possible but falls back cleanly to OpenRouter-hosted models.

Document the canonical DB-backed asset loop clearly: supported game schemas seed into Payload, canonical data edits round-trip through export/publish, the assistant shell lives inside the hosted UI, and the game remains the primary consumer.

Close the useful Asset Explorer/editor lane once the game-specific forms/assets + hosted assistant shell are coherent enough, then return active development focus to gameplay/content authored with coding agents.

Stand up the reviewable testing surface for Asset Explorer/game/schema/codegen work: strong unit coverage, browser-mode UI/component tests, deterministic Playwright E2E/visual flows, and a docs-site page that summarizes current results for fast human review.

Reduce alignment churn with concrete mass-update mechanisms instead of relying on AI for routine API drift: shared route clients/types, generated schemas/contracts, codemod-ready helpers, and central test fixtures/report parsers.

Publish the latest docs-site game/test review surface to GitHub Pages on each main-branch commit: promote CI artifacts into page-friendly data, surface latest status/coverage/report links in the docs UI, and keep commit-specific raw artifacts available through Actions for deeper debugging.

Unblock predictable public-build verification by reducing or decomposing the docs-site production compile surface. This is now materially addressed by removing the legacy docs/report/content-pack host routes, switching the main build to Turbopack, setting the workspace root explicitly, and stopping the Payload UI/plugin packages from being externalized.

Remove RepoPlanner/planning cockpit ownership from docs-site: strip planning navigation and host-side planning API/chat routes, remove leftover legacy docs/env/admin sync surfaces that do not serve the new portal, leave planner behavior to the RepoPlanner submodule/app, and sharpen docs-site into the DungeonBreak marketing plus internal admin/customer portal.

Define and implement the first internal-only auth posture for docs-site: explicit allowed-email access, minimal early roles, branded internal mailboxes, a temporary onboarding password, and a proxy gate that funnels the portal through a single login surface.

decision.summary: Phase 63 should continue only where it improves Escape the Dungeon authoring, inspection, balance, and play-loop support; generic product ambitions stay secondary.
decision.impact: The next editor work is justified only when it helps the real game content pipeline, which keeps the team out of another open-ended tooling detour.

decision.summary: The editor should become a hosted AI product. The chat surface lives in the UI, prefers existing user subscriptions where practical, but must still work when we provide the model path ourselves through OpenRouter or a similar hosted gateway.
decision.impact: This keeps the editor self-contained and usable in-browser while still letting us opportunistically reduce cost/friction with external subscriptions when integrations allow it.

decision.summary: The assistant chat is for planning, review, and targeted updates to forms/assets. Bulk schema/content authoring still remains viable through coding agents working directly in the repo.
decision.impact: The assistant shell stays lightweight and supportive instead of replacing the main development workflow.

decision.summary: Media generation stays inside Asset Explorer instead of living only in Payload admin. Schema annotations should declare media slots, the widget should queue real hosted generation where available, and unresolved media kinds such as video should still round-trip through explicit slot metadata instead of disappearing from the authoring model.
decision.impact: Asset JSON remains the source of truth for generated media relationships, and future media backends can be added behind the same form/widget contract without changing authored schema shapes again.

decision.summary: Asset Explorer should default to the actual Escape the Dungeon supported schema catalog. Manual schema creation remains available, but only as an advanced escape hatch when the game truly needs a new form.
decision.impact: The editor feels like a game content tool again instead of a generic schema workbench, which gets us back to shipping content and gameplay faster.

decision.summary: The planning snapshot/rollup should eventually treat `deferred` work as closed enough for current-lane progress reporting, or otherwise surface a separate effective-progress metric.
decision.impact: Phase progress will better match reality when non-critical work is intentionally parked instead of continuing to drag the percentage down.

decision.summary: Keep Playwright as the deterministic baseline for end-to-end and visual regression, use Vitest for fast unit coverage plus browser-mode UI/component tests, and treat AI-browser tooling such as Stagehand as optional exploratory assistance for volatile workflows rather than the primary assertion runner.
decision.impact: We keep a stable, debuggable, cost-controlled test pyramid while still leaving room for AI-assisted browser tooling where it saves time instead of introducing flake into the main gate.

decision.summary: For keeping forms/assets/game/codegen aligned, prefer generated route/types/schema clients, shared test fixtures, and codemod-capable helpers over relying on chat agents for repetitive repo-wide API updates.
decision.impact: Mass changes stay cheap, reviewable, and deterministic, with AI helping at the edges instead of becoming the only alignment mechanism.

decision.summary: The public, current review surface for the game/editor/testing stack should live on GitHub Pages and update on every main-branch commit. Actions artifacts remain the deep-dive source for commit-specific logs, HTML reports, and large attachments.
decision.impact: The team can always inspect the latest playable/docs-site state and test health without opening Actions first, while preserving richer per-run artifacts for debugging.

decision.summary: The static review-site host remains the public review surface, but the main docs-site production build is no longer a mystery stall. The practical fix was to slim the host down to the portal/asset-authoring surface, switch to Turbopack, point Next at the workspace root explicitly, and stop externalizing Payload packages that pull CSS.
decision.impact: Public review publishing stays separate and simple, while the real docs-site app can now build fast enough to stay in the normal verification loop.

decision.summary: Docs-site is the primary DungeonBreak web product, not a mixed host/planner shell. RepoPlanner/planning cockpit behavior should move out of the host app and live with the RepoPlanner submodule/app.
decision.impact: The main site can focus on marketing, game surfaces, internal admin/customer workflows, and content operations without carrying unrelated planner UX/API debt.

decision.summary: The site remains internal for now: only explicit allowed emails should log in. Public visitors can still see marketing/game-facing surfaces, but authenticated portal capabilities stay restricted.
decision.impact: This keeps the product usable for internal operations without pretending the portal is ready for open signup or broader customer access.

decision.summary: The first internal login is intentionally lightweight: allowlisted emails plus a temporary shared onboarding password are enough to mint a Payload session and separate portal-access cookie until a stronger internal auth provider is worth the cost.
decision.impact: The team can use the real portal immediately without leaving authoring blocked on a full auth product integration, while the allowlist still keeps the surface private.

decision.summary: Legacy Payload docs, env-comparison, and local-sync utilities do not belong in the main portal build unless they directly support Asset Explorer or media workflows.
decision.impact: Removing those routes, components, and generated references keeps the docs-site build graph smaller and lowers the chance that dead admin surfaces re-break typecheck or production builds.
